module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph
open Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The maximum cardinality among all independent sets `s`
    that maximize the quantity `|s| - |N(s)|`, where `N(s)`
    is the neighborhood of the set `s`. -/
noncomputable def aprime (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  letI indep_sets : Finset (Finset α) := univ.powerset.filter (fun s => G.IsIndepSet (s : Set α))
  letI diff (s : Finset α) : ℤ := (s.card : ℤ) - (⋃ v ∈ (s : Set α), G.neighborSet v).toFinset.card
  letI max_diff := (indep_sets.image diff).max
  letI critical_sets := indep_sets.filter (fun s ↦ diff s = max_diff.getD 0)
  letI max_card := (critical_sets.image Finset.card).max
  (max_card.getD 0 : ℝ)

/-- Independence number of the neighbourhood of `v`. -/
noncomputable def indepNeighborsCard (G : SimpleGraph α) (v : α) : ℕ :=
  (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).indepNum

/-- The same quantity as a real number. -/
noncomputable def indepNeighbors (G : SimpleGraph α) (v : α) : ℝ :=
  (indepNeighborsCard G v : ℝ)

/-- Average of `indepNeighbors` over all vertices. -/
noncomputable def averageIndepNeighbors (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ :=
  (∑ v ∈ Finset.univ, indepNeighbors G v) / (Fintype.card α : ℝ)

/-- Abbreviation for the average independence number of the neighborhoods.
-/
noncomputable abbrev l (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ := averageIndepNeighbors G

/-- The same quantity under a different name, used in some conjectures.
-/
noncomputable abbrev l_avg (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ := averageIndepNeighbors G

/-- Computable independence number via powerset enumeration. -/
def computable_indep_num (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.powerset.filter (fun s : Finset α =>
    ∀ u ∈ s, ∀ v ∈ s, u ≠ v → ¬G.Adj u v)).sup Finset.card

/-- Equivalence between computable and noncomputable independence number. -/
theorem indep_num_eq_computable (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    G.indepNum = computable_indep_num G := by
  unfold SimpleGraph.indepNum SimpleGraph.computable_indep_num
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply csSup_le
    · refine ⟨0, ∅, ?_, rfl⟩
      simp [SimpleGraph.IsIndepSet]
    · rintro n ⟨s, hs⟩
      calc n = s.card := hs.card_eq.symm
        _ ≤ _ := Finset.le_sup ?_
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset]
      exact ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun u hu v hv huv =>
        hs.isIndepSet (Finset.mem_coe.mpr hu) (Finset.mem_coe.mpr hv) huv⟩
  · apply Finset.sup_le
    intro s hs
    apply le_csSup
    · exact ⟨Fintype.card α, fun n ⟨s, hs⟩ => hs.card_eq ▸ s.card_le_univ⟩
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      exact ⟨s, ⟨fun x hx y hy hne =>
        (Finset.mem_filter.mp hs).2 x (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx) y (Finset.mem_coe.mp hy) hne,
        rfl⟩⟩

/-- Maximum local independence number over all vertices.
    For each vertex, we compute the independence number of the subgraph
    induced by its neighbors, and take the maximum over all vertices. -/
noncomputable def maxLocalIndependence (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ :=
  let locals := Finset.univ.image (fun v => (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).indepNum)
  (locals.max).getD 0

/-- Minimum local independence number over all vertices.
    For each vertex, we compute the independence number of the subgraph
    induced by its neighbors, and take the minimum over all vertices. -/
noncomputable def minLocalIndependence (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ :=
  let locals := Finset.univ.image (fun v => (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).indepNum)
  (locals.min).getD 0


end SimpleGraph

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture133.lean, the use of `(⌊l G⌋ : ℝ) ^ cC4` depends on interpreting the source's square brackets as a floor. The library's `SimpleGraph.l` correctly returns the unrounded neighborhood-independence average. The source appears instead to use brackets for grouping: it documents the floor operation separately as `FLOOR[x]`, and conjecture 133's definitions popup does not reference that operation. This choice changes the operand even on permitted graphs: for P₃, I verified in Lean that `l G = 4/3`, whereas its floor is 1. I have not established non-equivalence of the complete graph statements, so this is a questionable interpretation, not a confirmed misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaViña, WOWII, all.html, conjecture 133: `path(G) ≥ rad(G) + [average of λ(v)]^χ_C4`. Its popup calls `printDefinitions(35,13,4,73,0)`. In wowIIdefs.js, entry 4 defines the ordinary average of local independence numbers, while entry 22 separately defines `FLOOR[x]`. Read through https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html and the corresponding archived wowIIdefs.js.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the bracket convention with the source. If the brackets are grouping, replace `(⌊l G⌋ : ℝ) ^ cC4` with `(l G) ^ cC4` and remove the docstring's assertion of a standard floor convention. Otherwise, supply a reference establishing that interpretation or a contextual equivalence proof.

findings.description: The anonymous sanity check at FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture13.lean:53–56 incorrectly says that `indepNeighborsCard` at a vertex of K₂ is 0 because its singleton neighborhood has 'no independent edges'. Independence number counts vertices, not edges: this value is 1. The example actually proves only `maxDegree = 1`. I proved `indepNeighborsCard (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) 0 = 1` in Lean. Neither the library definition nor the main conjecture has this error.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII definitions 4 and 5 define local independence as the independence number of the neighbor-induced subgraph, and independence number as the maximum number of pairwise nonadjacent vertices. A singleton therefore has independence number 1. This also follows from Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique's `IsIndepSet` and `indepNum` definitions.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the docstring with 'In K₂, the maximum degree is 1.' If a neighborhood-independence sanity check is wanted, add a separate example asserting that its value is 1.

reformulations.difference: The source defines criticality by comparison with every independent set, followed by maximizing cardinality. Lean implements two finite maximizations, using `getD 0` at each stage, and returns the result as a real number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The independent-set family contains the empty set, so its finite set of signed deficiencies has an attained maximum. Consequently, the critical-set family is also nonempty, and its cardinality maximum is attained. Neither default changes the value. In characterizations.lean I proved `G.aprime = (k : ℝ) ↔ ∃ s, Critical G s ∧ s.card = k ∧ ∀ t, Critical G t → t.card ≤ k`, with Critical using precisely the source's universally quantified deficiency comparison.

reformulations.difference: Lean enumerates the powerset, filters by explicit pairwise nonadjacency, and takes a natural-number `Finset.sup`, rather than using the usual maximum-independent-set definition or Mathlib's `sSup` definition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The filter predicate is definitionally equivalent to `G.IsIndepSet (s : Set α)`. Finiteness bounds every eligible cardinality by `Fintype.card α`, and the empty set supplies cardinality zero. The file proves equality with Mathlib's `G.indepNum`; I checked that proof and proved the corresponding equality-of-values iff in use_site_checks.lean. Empty and singleton cases were also checked.

reformulations.difference: The source assumes that the maximum local independence number of the complement is at most 1. Lean assumes the bound separately for every vertex.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite nonempty vertex set, a maximum is at most 1 exactly when every value is at most 1; the source's n ≥ 5 guarantees nonemptiness. In characterizations.lean I proved the more general `G.maxLocalIndependence ≤ k ↔ ∀ v, indepNeighborsCard G v ≤ k`, which specializes to the complement and k = 1.

reformulations.difference: The quotient lower bound for the induced-tree size is expressed by cross-multiplication, with an explicit positive-denominator hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The denominator is a natural-valued minimum local independence number. Where the source's quotient is defined, it is positive. Under that condition, `2 * (e : ℝ) / m ≤ t` is equivalent to `2 * e ≤ t * m`; this exact arithmetic iff was proved in use_site_checks.lean. The minimum is taken over a nonempty finite vertex set, and the source explicitly applies it to the complement.

could_not_verify: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture133.conjecture133: the bracket/floor interpretation underlying the questionable finding remains unsettled; I did not prove equivalence or non-equivalence of the complete graph predicates.

WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141.conjecture141: its local-independence component agrees with the source, but I did not settle the separate girth/rounding conventions. The source writes the exact term `(1/2)*girth`, whereas Lean uses integer division and assigns girth 0 to acyclic graphs. The consulted source definition does not specify an acyclic value, and a complete contextual equivalence check was not established.
review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defect was found in the nine definitions/abbreviations or the proved theorem of Independence.lean itself. Checked open versus closed neighborhoods, signed deficiency, attainment of both critical-set maxima, finite versus set cardinalities, casts, and empty/singleton inputs. Lean tests include edgeless and complete graphs, P₃, and C₅. I also proved positivity of the neighborhood average for connected nontrivial finite graphs, ruling out a zero denominator at the use site in conjecture 58. The vertex-local wrappers retain no finiteness instance and inherit Mathlib.indepNum's natural-valued totalization: on an infinite star the center's value is 0 despite arbitrarily large independent subsets in its neighborhood. This was verified in infinite.lean; all current use sites are finite, so it does not change their claims. The live WOWII HTTPS endpoint was unavailable; archived primary-source pages were used. All four final Lean experiment files under /workspace/review/ compile without errors or warnings and use no sorry axioms. The target file remains byte-identical to the committed version.
